title: Change of topology detects finite type of arbitrary modules
statement: Let $X$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\epsilon_X:(X_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_{X,\mathrm{et}})\to(X_{\mathrm{Zar}},\mathcal O_X)$ be the canonical ringed-site morphism with tensor module pullback [lem-trf-zariski-etale-functor-comparison-square]. Let $F$ be any sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. On either site, finite type means that on a covering of every object the module is generated by finitely many sections, equivalently it admits an epimorphism from a finite free structure module there. Then $F$ is of finite type on $X_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ if and only if $\epsilon_X^*F$ is of finite type on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$. No quasi-coherence, Noetherian condition or quasi-compactness is assumed.

proof.text: Suppose $F$ is of finite type. On a Zariski open cover choose epimorphisms $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to F|_U$. The module pullback is left adjoint by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction], so it preserves cokernels and finite coproducts. Its tensor formula sends $\mathcal O_U$ to $\mathcal O_{U,\mathrm{et}}$ by $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$, with inverse $a\mapsto a\otimes1$. It therefore sends each chosen epimorphism to an epimorphism from a finite free structure module. The open cover remains an etale cover, and after any etale test object its base changes still cover, by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. This is exactly finite type on the etale site.

Conversely assume $\epsilon_X^*F$ is of finite type and fix $x\in X$. Choose an etale chart $X'\to X$ whose image contains $x$, on which finitely many sections $s_1,\ldots,s_n$ generate the restricted module. By [lem-trf-zariski-etale-tensor-sections], $\epsilon_X^*F$ is the sheafification of $P(V\xrightarrow f X)=\Gamma(V,f^*F)$, naturally also on module maps. The sheafification unit $P\to P^\#$ becomes an isomorphism after sheafification, by the universal property [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-iso-locally-bijective] to this unit: every $s_i$ locally lifts to $P$. Successively refine for the finitely many $i$ and choose a chart above a point of $X'$ over $x$. Thus on one etale $f':V'\to X$, still meeting the fibre over $x$, all the $s_i$ are represented by sections $g_i\in\Gamma(V',f'^*F)$. The restricted $s_i$ still generate, by the local meaning of generation.

Choose $z\in V'$ over $x$. By [def-pc-module-pullback], $f'^*F$ is the sheafified tensor of $f'^{-1}F$ and $\mathcal O_{V'}$, and its inverse-image factor is the sheafification of the presheaf of neighbourhood colimits. For each of these two sheafifications, the unit becomes an isomorphism on sheafifying, and hence has local lifts by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-iso-locally-bijective]. First shrink to a Zariski neighbourhood of $z$ where each $g_i$ is a finite sum $\sum_j a_{ij}\otimes r_{ij}$. Shrink again so every $r_{ij}$ lifts to the presheaf inverse image. Each such presheaf section is represented by some $t_{ij}\in F(U_{ij})$ with $U_{ij}$ an open neighbourhood of the image of the chosen source open. This representative exists because the neighbourhood index is filtered, with intersections as common refinements. There are only finitely many terms. Intersect the $U_{ij}$ to obtain an open $U\ni x$ and replace the source by its intersection with $f'^{-1}U$. We obtain a Zariski open $V''\subseteq V'$ containing $z$, on which $s_i=\sum_j a_{ij}\,\epsilon_X^*t_{ij}$, with all $t_{ij}\in F(U)$.

The map $V''\to X$ is etale: $V''$ is a Zariski open of an etale chart, so it is an object in the small etale site. An etale map is flat and locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism], so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open] shows its image $W$ is open. We have $x\in W\subseteq U$; restrict all the $t_{ij}$ to $W$. Let $N$ be their finite number and let $q:\mathcal O_W^{\oplus N}\to F|_W$ send its basis vectors to them. On $V''$ the images of these vectors under $\epsilon_W^*q$ span each $s_i$, by the displayed formulas of step 3; therefore they generate there. Since $V''\to W$ is a surjective etale cover, local generation there implies $\epsilon_W^*q$ is an epimorphism on $W_{\mathrm{et}}$. Explicitly, a section of the target first lifts locally to a linear combination of the $s_i$ and then to the corresponding combination of the $t_{ij}$. This is local surjectivity, which implies epimorphy by [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective]; module epimorphy is equivalent to this underlying abelian assertion because cokernels are sheafified sectionwise cokernels [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

For each $y\in W$ choose a geometric point $\bar y$ above it and put $R=\mathcal O_{W,y}$. Exactness of geometric stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] makes $(\epsilon_W^*q)_{\bar y}$ surjective. The natural module comparison [lem-sfb-etale-zariski-module-geometric-stalk] identifies this map with $q_y\otimes_R R^{\mathrm{sh}}$, where the chosen separable closure of $\kappa(y)$ in the geometric field defines $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$. The canonical local map $R\to R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is faithfully flat by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-faithfully-flat], in particular flat. Applying the surjectivity-reflection clause of [lem-pc-local-flat-faithful-flat-reflects-surjective] to this flat local map gives surjectivity of $q_y$. Thus $q$ is surjective on every ordinary stalk. By [lem-sc-abelian-sheaf-epi-iff-stalk-epi] and the cokernel description in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], $q$ is an epimorphism of $\mathcal O_W$-modules. This is the faithful-flatness check in 08HD, expressed with the existing geometric-stalk comparison rather than ordinary stalks on $V''$.

For every $x$ we have produced an open neighbourhood $W$ and an epimorphism $\mathcal O_W^{\oplus N}\to F|_W$. These opens cover $X$, so $F$ is of finite type by the definition in the statement. If $X$ is empty, the empty cover proves both conditions; if there are no generators, the same argument uses $N=0$ and proves the module is zero locally. No finiteness property of $X$ and no quasi-coherence of $F$ entered the argument.
